high.title: IPCA-15: Inflation Preview Advances 0.62% in May, Above Expectations, and Breaches Central Bank's 4.5% Ceiling Target
high.summary: Brazil's inflation preview (IPCA-15) rose 0.62% in May, exceeding market expectations of 0.56% and pushing the 12-month accumulated rate to 4.64%, breaching the Central Bank's 4.5% ceiling target. The monthly reading decelerated from April's 0.89% but accelerated on an annual basis from 4.37%. Food and beverages led with 1.38% variation, followed by Housing (1.03%) and Health/Personal Care (1.05%). This above-target inflation reading increases pressure on BCB to maintain or potentially raise the Selic rate at upcoming COPOM meetings. For BRL traders, higher inflation typically supports BRL strength through expectations of tighter monetary policy, though fiscal concerns may limit this effect. Bond investors should expect higher yields as markets price in extended restrictive monetary policy. The breach of the inflation target ceiling is particularly significant as it may force BCB to adopt a more hawkish stance, impacting both FX and fixed income markets.

high.title: Ibovespa Rises with New Wave of Middle East Optimism and Ignores Above-Expected IPCA-15; 5 Things to Know Before Investing Today (27)
high.summary: The Ibovespa tracked improving international sentiment with news of progress in US-Iran peace negotiations, with optimism overshadowing reactions to above-expected IPCA-15 inflation. By 10:10 AM, the index was up 0.47% at 177,420 points. USD/BRL moved against the grain of global dollar weakness, rising 0.53% to R$ 5.0538, while DXY fell 0.10%. The inflation preview breaching the 4.5% ceiling target creates a complex scenario for markets - while geopolitical optimism supported equities, the BRL weakened despite inflation above target, suggesting market focus on external factors over domestic monetary policy implications. This divergence between strong inflation data and BRL weakness indicates investors may be pricing in other concerns such as fiscal policy or global risk appetite. For equity investors, the Ibovespa's resilience despite inflation concerns suggests continued foreign interest, while FX traders should monitor whether domestic fundamentals reassert dominance over external sentiment.

medium.title: Ibovespa Loses Strength Amid Geopolitical Uncertainties and Data Battery; 5 Things to Know Before Investing Today (28)
medium.summary: The Ibovespa attempted to recover previous session losses with rising oil prices amid renewed US-Iran uncertainties. The index oscillated from +0.21% to -0.36% by 10:30 AM. USD/BRL fell 0.13% to R$ 5.0543, aligning with global dollar weakness as DXY dropped 0.05%. Brazil's unemployment rate hit a record low of 5.8% for the April quarter, supporting the economic outlook but potentially adding to inflation pressures through tight labor markets.

medium.title: Unemployment Rate Reaches 5.8% in Quarter Through April 2026, Lowest for Period in Historical Series
medium.summary: Brazil's unemployment rate fell to 5.8% in the quarter through April, down from 6.1% in March and marking the lowest rate for an April quarter since the series began in 2012. The rate dropped 0.8 percentage points year-over-year from 6.6%. Market expectations were for 5.9%. The tight labor market supports economic growth but may fuel wage inflation, potentially complicating BCB's inflation targeting efforts.

medium.title: Raízen (RAIZ4), Petrobras (PETR4), Azul (AZUL3) and Other Highlights for Wednesday (27)
medium.summary: Raízen advances debt restructuring talks for R$ 65 billion obligations, with creditors demanding new funding for sustainable recovery. Agreement deadline is June 9, requiring 50%+1 creditor approval. Petrobras responded about interest in Refit land, while Azul debuted on NYSE. These corporate developments affect major Ibovespa components, with Raízen's debt resolution particularly important for energy sector stability.

medium.title: US GDP Slows to 1.6% in Q1 2026, While Consumer Inflation Remains Elevated
medium.summary: US GDP was revised down to 1.6% annualized in Q1 2026 from initial 2% reading, though improving from Q4 2025's 0.5%. The slowdown was driven by exports, investment, consumer spending, and government expenditure, partially offset by higher imports. This US economic deceleration may affect global risk sentiment and impact Brazilian asset flows, particularly if it influences Federal Reserve policy expectations.
